summary: Embedded dashboard iframe applies incorrect org-level filters after auto-refresh, exposing mismatched telemetry
summary_verbose: Customer reports that an embedded dashboard (iframe) used on their internal portal shows metrics scoped to the visiting org after the dashboard auto-refresh completes. The embed was configured to pin filters to the customer's org (org_id param in embed token), but after 1-2 automatic refreshes the visible filter switches to the embedding user's organization scope, causing confusion and potential exposure of unrelated org-level rollups.
description:
Issue summary:
BrightLens embedded our session metrics dashboard into their internal support portal using the standard signed-embed token with org_id pinned. On initial load the dashboard respects the pinned org filter (customer org), but after one or two automatic refresh cycles (interval=60s) the dashboard resets to the viewer's org filter (the internal staffer in BrightLens), which in some cases shows aggregated telemetry from both BrightLens and their partner tenants.

Impact:
- Customer-facing risk: internal analytics pages temporarily show metrics not scoped to the intended org (confidentiality concern).
- Operational: dashboards used for SLA and billing audits are unreliable during refresh windows.
- Business: BrightLens is an enterprise-tier customer; this is a potential data isolation concern.

Environment:
- Console: production, us-east-1 region
- Dashboard: "Session Usage — Top Routes" (dashboard id: dash_44b1)
- Embed method: signed iframe token (embed_v2), auto-refresh interval 60s

Steps to reproduce:
1) BrightLens creates signed embed token with claim org_id=org_brightlens and dashboard_id=dash_44b1.
2) Navigate to the portal page that hosts the iframe (viewer is a BrightLens staff account bound to org_staff_BLens).
3) Observe dashboard loads correctly showing org_brightlens scoped metrics.
4) Wait for 1-2 automatic refresh cycles (dashboard refresh every 60s).
5) After refresh, filters in the dashboard UI show org=org_staff_BLens and the visible metrics change.

Expected behavior:
Pinned org filter from the embed token should be persistent and immutable from the viewer's session; auto-refresh should not re-evaluate the viewer's session scope.

Actual behavior:
Auto-refresh flow triggers a server-side filter merge that prioritizes the current session's org over embed-level pinned org. This causes the dashboard UI to display the viewer's org filter after refresh.

Logs / traces / evidence:
- Customer screenshot (attached) showing initial and post-refresh filter values and delta in totals.
- Console trace id: trace:console-embed-20260312-9a7b (collected from BrightLens repro session).
- Frontend console shows a 200 response from /api/dashboard/data with payload containing filters: {"org": "org_staff_BLens"} at timestamp 2026-03-12T15:04:11Z.
- Auth logs show viewer session org claim org_staff_BLens valid; embed token check returns org_brightlens as pinned in token validation step.

Temporary workaround:
Advise BrightLens to increase refresh interval to a large value (e.g., 24h) and avoid embedding in pages where their internal staff will authenticate with their own Redwood session. They should instead create a dedicated service account to view the embed if feasible. Support provided steps to regenerate embed with longer expiry.

Notes on customer communication:
- First contact (2026-03-12): collected reproduction steps and screenshot.
- Customer asked for priority handling due to audit needs this week.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 18:00 - Reproduced internally with a test embed token: observed same behavior when developer portal session exists (repro user with independent org).
Hypothesis A: front-end refresh code applies a merge: embedFilters + sessionFilters -> session wins when keys collide. This was introduced in embed refresh refactor (PR 1490).

Hypothesis B: server variant of /api/dashboard/data honors session cookies on background refresh requests and ignores embed token on subsequent refresh if embed token is not re-sent. We saw that iframe background refresh uses the browser session and sends cookies, but the initial load used embed token in query param.

Initial triage: reproduced by toggling the embed to use query param vs Authorization header; behavior differs. When embed token is in Authorization header for every data request the pinned org holds; when token is only used on initial page load the session cookie takes precedence on subsequent refresh calls.
Relevant commits: console/embed: refresh flow refactor (commit a7b3f2) and PR 1542 implementing token caching in frontend.

2026-03-12 20:10 - Engineering (Diego Alvarez): Reproduced locally with minimal app. Confirmed server endpoints accept either embed token in Authorization header or browser session cookie. Background refresh was not re-attaching embed Authorization header. Likely front-end bug.

root_cause: Frontend refresh path for embedded dashboards was refactored to reuse browser session cookies for background polling but failed to persist the signed embed token on subsequent data requests. As a result, the server merged session-scoped filters with embed-scoped filters and session scope took precedence.
resolution: Engineering merged hotfix PR that re-attaches the embed token (Authorization header) on every dashboard data request originating from a signed embed. Hotfix deployed to prod us-east-1 on 2026-03-13 02:30 UTC. Added unit/integration tests covering embed token propagation and established a telemetry alert to detect any future divergence in filter scopes.
resolution_notes: Deployed hotfix (PR 1542) to prod us-east-1. Verified with BrightLens on a test page; post-deploy the embed maintained pinned org after multiple refresh cycles. Follow-up: add e2e embedding test in CI and update embed docs to recommend Authorization header usage when refresh is enabled.

Update embed docs to call out recommended token propagation best practices
Run org-scope audit for other dashboard refresh flows (owner: dashboard-team)
Add a console alert that fires if a dashboard shows a different org scope on refresh than on load (alert rule id: TBD)
